subject: Hosted to Dedicated migration: capacity checklist & cutover windows
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@streamly.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration inquiry (Streamly)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the hosted support so far — we've hit a scale inflection and want to start planning a migration to Dedicated capacity. High level: currently on Redwood hosted API using r-llama3-70b for chat; avg concurrent requests ~85, median response length ~450 tokens, peak sustained requests observed ~280 QPS during marketing campaign spikes (attached summary).

What we need from Redwood:
- Validation of the GPU sizing you recommend given these numbers (we care about latency P95 < 600ms for 512-token responses).
- A proposed cutover timeline with minimal impact to production (we prefer a staged canary).
- Any requirements for data plane changes (VPC, egress, KMS).
- Expected downtime or rollback plan; fallback to hosted API is ideal.

We attached our usage export (streamly-usage-summary.csv). Can we get a capacity check and a rough timeline? We are hoping to align this with our Nov marketing push.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
CTO, Streamly
priya@streamly.io
Attachment: streamly-usage-summary.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya@streamly.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration inquiry (Streamly)

Hi Priya — thanks for the details and the usage export. High level: we can definitely support a migration with a staged canary and fallback to hosted while we validate. Next steps on our side:

- I'll run an initial sizing pass with engineering + solutions (Marissa cc'd).
- Please fill the attached short questionnaire so we can confirm request size distribution and long tail (the CSV helped but we need a little more breakdown).
- Proposed kickoff call: Thu 10/30 10am PT — does that work?

Preliminary notes from a quick pass: with your peaks (280 QPS) and median token counts, a safe initial Dedicated pool is likely 4 x A100-80GB or 6 x A10x GPUs depending on model variants + quantization. We will supply a precise GPU-hour estimate once we validate cache hit rates and request concurrency patterns.

I've attached a short questionnaire (initial_capacity_questionnaire.pdf) and will follow up with a draft action plan after the call.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted -> Dedicated migration inquiry (Streamly) — sizing validation request

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Priya's thread and the usage export. Ask: can you validate the quick estimate I wrote in my reply and produce a short checklist of tests we need before cutover? Key constraints: P95 < 600ms for 512 tokens, staged canary preferred, fallback path to hosted API required.

Quick context and guesses to validate:
- Customer model: r-llama3-70b (float16 production variant); they may accept int8/4 quantized variant for cost savings if quality checks pass.
- Observed peak: 280 QPS sustained over 10–15 minute windows; average concurrency ~85.
- Token distribution: median 450, long tail to 2k.

Initial sizing hypothesis (for validation):
- Option A (latency-first): 4 x A100-80GB with 2 concurrent model replicas + autoscale headroom for burst to 6 instances (target P95 margin).
- Option B (cost-first): 6 x A10 with quantized 4-bit model variants and aggressive prefix caching; expect slightly higher P95 but lower TCO.

Please validate kernel/memory constraints for Llama-3-70b variants, check KV cache hit-rate assumptions from the CSV, and confirm whether continuous batching will be required or if we can rely on low-latency single-request paths.

Proposed cutover timeline (we can tighten after validation):
- Staging prep & infra provisioning: Nov 5–7
- Staging smoke test (internal): Nov 8 (6–12 hour window)
- Canary (10% traffic): Nov 9 morning -> monitor 4 hours
- Canary (50%): Nov 9 afternoon -> monitor 6 hours
- Full cutover: Nov 10 after final checks

Attachments to produce: capacity_calc_v1.xlsx (I will draft and attach) and a Mutual Action Plan doc for signatures. Also need: SSO accounts for Streamly engineers, KMS key ARN if they want customer-managed keys.

Please add technical checklist items, infra tickets, and a recommended rollback window.

Thanks,
-Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted -> Dedicated migration inquiry (Streamly) — sizing validation request

Thanks for the context — did a quick sync with Infra and Runtime teams. Notes below (quoting your hypotheses):

- Model memory: r-llama3-70b float16 requires ~67GB GPU RAM for optimal receptive context at 2048 tokens; int8 quant reduces memory but will increase inference overhead. A100-80GB fits the float16 comfortably. A10s will need sharded execution; expect ~10–15% higher latency.
- Cache assumptions: if we can get prefix/KV cache hit > 40% (customer said they have many repeated prompts during campaigns), we can shave effective QPS by ~30%. Request that Priya confirm % of repeated prompts (questionnaire item).
- Continuous batching: recommended for cost-control but must be throttled to preserve P95. We'll enable adaptive batching with a 50ms window during the canary.

Updated recommendation:
- Staging: 2 x A100-80GB (for smoke tests, dev infra)
- Initial Dedicated pool (canary-ready): 3 x A100-80GB + autoscale policy to add up to 6 instances on sustained >70% utilization for 10m windows. This gives margin for caching warmups and model rollouts.
- Fallback: traffic split can be handled at the routing layer; we will keep the hosted API route active and set a 5-minute automatic rollback trigger on error rate regressions.

Cutover cadence (operationalized):
- Nov 5–7: Provision infra, configure VPC peering and KMS dummy test key, populate staging model.
- Nov 8 02:00–08:00 PT: Staging smoke run (internal) — validate latencies, KV hit-rate, and memory.
- Nov 9 06:00 PT: Canary 10% (monitoring: latency, error-rate, token-cost burn).
- Nov 9 12:00 PT: Canary 50% (if metrics stable -> proceed).
- Nov 10 00:00–04:00 PT: Full cutover (low-traffic window).

Operational asks for Sales / Customer:
- Mutual Action Plan signed by Nov 3.
- Streamly to provide KMS key ARN and at least two SSO test accounts by Nov 4.
- Provide a traffic ramp playbook (how they will shift 10->50->100%).

Infra ticket created: INF-2026-991 (provision A100 pool for DL-2026-783). I'll attach capacity_calc_v1.xlsx once I get the final CSV breakdown.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment placeholder: capacity_calc_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 64KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya@streamly.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration inquiry (Streamly) — proposed plan and dates

Priya — summarizing final plan and asks so we can lock dates:

Plan summary:
- Staging infra provision & verification: Nov 5–8 (internal)
- Canary rollout: Nov 9 (10% -> 50% over the day)
- Full cutover: Nov 10 (early morning low-traffic window)
- Dedicated pool: 3 x A100-80GB, autoscale to 6 instances on sustained >70% utilization (can revise if you opt for quantized variant).
- Fallback: Hosted API route remains active; router rollback threshold = 5% error-rate increase or 2x baseline latency regression at P95.

Customer asks (need by Nov 4):
- Sign the Mutual Action Plan: https://drive.redwood.com/streams/DL-2026-783/migration-plan
- Provide KMS key ARN or confirm Redwood-managed key (we default to Redwood-managed if you don't provide an ARN).
- Create two SSO test accounts (ops+eng) and share access details with marissa@redwood.com.
- Respond on preference: latency-first (A100 pool) or cost-first (A10 + quant) so we finalize procurement.

If you approve, we'll open the procurement POs and schedule Infra engineers for provisioning on Nov 5. We can also compress schedule by 48 hours if Streamly signs the MAP today.

Best,
-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (DOCX, 32KB)
